course_name_original: PRINCIPLES OF ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING
course_name_en: Principles of Electrical and Electronic Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: To learn the basic concepts related to the use of electrical energy.
To learn the working principles of various electrical and electronic systems.
Acquiring a general electrical engineering knowledge that may be required in business life.
Explains the structure, working principle, different connection types of direct current motors.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Basic concepts and units. Static electric; Coulomb and Ampere laws. Potential difference.
DC Circuits: Electric current. Ground concept. Resistors and Ohm’s Law. Power.
DC Circuits: Ideal voltage source. Current source. Serial and parallel connections. Circuit analysis by using loop current and node voltage equations.
DC Circuits: Thevenin equivalent circuit and superposition principle.
AC Circuits: Alternating current concept. Types of alternating current. Frequency, period, amplitude and phase concepts. Average and effective values.
AC Circuits: Alternating current concept. Types of alternating current. Frequency, period, amplitude and phase concepts. Average and effective values.
AC Circuits: Capacitor and inductor components. Complex impedance. AC circuit analysis. Input impedance and power factor. Phase shifting.
1.Midterm, Energy Systems: Principles of electric energy generation and transmission. Transformers. Reactive power compensation. Grounding. Relays.
Electric Machinery: Electromechanic energy conversion. DC and AC motors and their control. Robots.
Analog Electronics: Diodes and transistors. Rectifiers.
Analog Electronics: Operational amplifiers. Comparators. Measurement circuits and sensors.
Digital Electronics: Boolean Algebra. Logic circuit components.
2. Midterm, Digital Electronics: Logic circuit design and applications.
Digital Electronics: Logic circuit design and applications.
bibliography: Aydemir, M.T., Nakiboğlu, C., Elektrik Devreleri, (Çeviri), Schaum Serisi
Rizzoni, G., Principles and Applications of Electrical Engineering, Mc Graw Hill
